blocks.text: Supplementary: radian (plane angle), steradian (solid angle). Derived: N = kg m s⁻², Pa = kg m⁻¹ s⁻², J = kg m² s⁻².
Prefixes: p 10⁻¹², n 10⁻⁹, μ 10⁻⁶, m 10⁻³, c 10⁻², k 10³, M 10⁶, G 10⁹.
km h⁻¹ → m s⁻¹: divide by 3.6 (72 km h⁻¹ = 20 m s⁻¹). 1 g cm⁻³ = 1000 kg m⁻³. 1 mm² = 10⁻⁶ m².

items: Sig figs: leading zeros never count (0.00520 → 3); trailing zeros after the point do; in a × 10ⁿ only a counts.
× or ÷: answer keeps the fewest sig figs; + or −: the fewest decimal places.
Systematic error (zero error, bad calibration): remove by correction. Random error: reduce by averaging many readings.
Precise = small absolute uncertainty; accurate = small percentage uncertainty.

blocks.text: g = 4π²l/T²: %g = %l + 2 × %T. Sphere volume: 3 × %r.
Homogeneity: every term added or equated must have the same dimensions. Check T = 2π√(l/g): √(L ÷ LT⁻²) = [T].
Dimensions cannot find pure numbers (½, 2π) or tell sin from cos; a dimensionally correct equation can still be wrong.

items: Components: Aₓ = A cos θ, A_y = A sin θ (θ from the +x-axis).
Resultant: R = √(Rₓ² + R_y²), θ = tan⁻¹(R_y/Rₓ).
Two vectors at angle θ: R² = A² + B² + 2AB cos θ.
Range: |A − B| ≤ R ≤ A + B.
Unit vector Â = A/|A|; position vector r = x î + y ĵ; null vector has zero magnitude.

blocks.text: tan⁻¹ alone gives the wrong quadrant: read it from the signs. Rₓ < 0, R_y > 0 → 2nd quadrant, θ = 180° − φ, where φ = tan⁻¹|R_y/Rₓ|.
Two equal vectors A at 120° give R = A; at 90°, R = √2 A.

head: Dot A·B
Cross A×B
rows: î×ĵ = k̂, ĵ×k̂ = î, k̂×î = ĵ, î×î = 0

blocks.text: Angle between vectors: cos θ = A·B/AB. |A×B| = area of the parallelogram on A and B.

title: Torque and the two conditions of equilibrium

items: Torque τ = rF sin θ = F × (perpendicular distance of its line from the axis). Unit N m.
Anticlockwise torque is taken positive, clockwise negative.
1st condition: ΣF = 0 (ΣFₓ = 0, ΣF_y = 0) → no linear acceleration.
2nd condition: Στ = 0 → no angular acceleration.
Static equilibrium: at rest. Dynamic: constant velocity or constant angular velocity.

blocks.text: A force whose line passes through the axis gives zero torque. The N m of torque is never written as joule.
Take torques about the point where an unknown force acts: that force drops out.

items: v_f = v_i + at
S = v_i t + ½at²
2aS = v_f² − v_i²
S = ½(v_i + v_f)t
Distance in the nth second: Sₙ = v_i + ½a(2n − 1)
Free fall: a = g = 9.8 m s⁻² downwards.

blocks.text: v–t graph: slope = acceleration, area under it = displacement. Distance–time graph: slope = speed.
Dropped from rest, distances in successive equal seconds go 1 : 3 : 5 : 7.
These hold only for constant acceleration. Take one direction as positive: g is then −9.8 m s⁻² for upward motion.

items: Momentum p = mv; unit kg m s⁻¹ = N s.
2nd law: F = Δp/Δt = ma (constant mass).
Impulse J = FΔt = Δp = area under a force–time graph.
3rd law: action and reaction are equal, opposite and act on different bodies, so they never cancel.
No external force → total momentum conserved: gun recoil mV = −m′v′.

blocks.text: A ball of speed v that bounces back with speed v has Δp = 2mv, not zero (direction reverses).
Same Δp over a longer Δt means a smaller force: crumple zones, bending knees on landing.
Elastic, 1-D, m₂ at rest: v₁ = (m₁ − m₂)u₁/(m₁ + m₂), v₂ = 2m₁u₁/(m₁ + m₂).

items: Equal masses: they exchange velocities.
Heavy hits light: light one moves off at about 2u₁.
Light hits heavy: light one bounces back at about u₁.

blocks.text: Elastic: speed of approach = speed of separation.

items: Time of flight T = 2v_i sin θ/g
Maximum height H = v_i² sin² θ/2g
Range R = v_i² sin 2θ/g; maximum R = v_i²/g at θ = 45°

blocks.text: Horizontal velocity v_i cos θ stays constant (no air resistance). Vertical velocity is zero at the top. Acceleration is g downwards all the time. The path is a parabola.
θ and (90° − θ) give the same range, e.g. 30° and 60°.
Range uses sin 2θ, height uses sin² θ. Speed at the top is v_i cos θ, not zero.

items: W = F·d = Fd cos θ; unit joule (N m).
Variable force: W = area under the force–displacement graph.
Power P = W/t = F·v; watt = J s⁻¹; 1 hp = 746 W.
1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J (a unit of energy, not power).
Conservative force (gravity, electric, spring): work independent of path, zero round a closed path. Non-conservative: friction, air drag.

blocks.text: W = 0 when F ⟂ d: centripetal force, carrying a bag horizontally. Friction opposite to motion does negative work.
Lifting at steady speed: P = mgv.

items: K.E. = ½mv² = p²/2m
P.E. near the Earth = mgh
Work–energy principle: net work = change in K.E.
Falling with friction f: mgh = ½mv² + fh
No friction: K.E. + P.E. = constant.

blocks.text: Speed after falling h from rest: v = √(2gh), whatever the mass.

title: Absolute potential energy and escape velocity

items: Absolute P.E. U = −GMm/r (zero at infinity, negative everywhere else).
g at the surface = GM/R², so GM = gR².
Escape velocity v_esc = √(2GM/R) = √(2gR) ≈ 11.2 km s⁻¹ for the Earth.

blocks.text: v_esc does not depend on the mass of the body or the direction it is thrown.
mgh holds only for h ≪ R. Raising m from the surface to a height R needs ΔU = ½mgR, not mgR.
A planet with the same density but twice the radius has twice the escape velocity (v_esc ∝ R√ρ).

items: θ = s/r (radians); 1 rev = 2π rad = 360°; 1 rad ≈ 57.3°.
ω = Δθ/Δt (rad s⁻¹); ω = 2πf = 2π/T.
α = Δω/Δt (rad s⁻²).
Links: v = rω, a_t = rα.
Same form as linear: ω_f = ω_i + αt, θ = ω_i t + ½αt², 2αθ = ω_f² − ω_i².

blocks.text: rev/min → rad s⁻¹: multiply by 2π/60. 60 rpm = 2π rad s⁻¹.
On a rigid rotating body every point has the same ω, but v = rω grows with r.

items: a_c = v²/r = rω², towards the centre.
F_c = mv²/r = mrω².
It is supplied by a real force: string tension, gravity (orbits), friction (car on a bend), electric force (electron round a nucleus).

blocks.text: F_c does no work (it is ⟂ to velocity), so speed stays constant in uniform circular motion. If the string breaks, the body moves off along the tangent.

title: Moment of inertia and angular momentum

head: Linear
Rotational
rows: L = Iω (kg m² s⁻¹ = J s)

blocks.text: I about the centre: hoop mr², disc ½mr², solid sphere ⅖mr², rod (1/12)mL².
No external torque → Iω constant. A diver or skater pulls in the arms: I falls, ω rises.
Rolling down height h: disc v = √(4gh/3) beats hoop v = √(gh); mass and radius don't matter.

items: Orbital speed v = √(GM/r); close to the Earth v = √(gR) ≈ 7.9 km s⁻¹.
Period T = 2π√(r³/GM), so T² ∝ r³.
Geostationary: T = 24 h, over the equator, moving with the Earth's spin, r ≈ 4.23 × 10⁴ km from the centre (about 36,000 km up).
Apparent weight in a lift: m(g + a) when accelerating upwards, m(g − a) when accelerating downwards; zero in free fall (weightlessness).
Artificial gravity: spin a station of radius R at f = (1/2π)√(g/R).

blocks.text: Orbital speed does not depend on the satellite's mass. v_esc = √2 × orbital speed for the same r.

items: Stokes' law (sphere): F = 6πηrv.
η unit: N s m⁻² = Pa s = kg m⁻¹ s⁻¹.
Terminal velocity (drag = weight): v_t = 2gr²ρ/9η.
Upthrust = weight of fluid displaced = ρ_fluid V g (Archimedes).
A body floats if its density ≤ the fluid's; fraction submerged = ρ_body/ρ_fluid.

blocks.text: The book's v_t ignores upthrust; with fluid density σ use (ρ − σ) in place of ρ.
v_t ∝ r²: a drop of twice the radius falls 4 times as fast. Viscosity of liquids falls as they warm.

items: Continuity: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂ (steady flow, incompressible fluid). Av = volume flow rate (m³ s⁻¹).
Bernoulli: P + ½ρv² + ρgh = constant along a streamline (each term in Pa = J m⁻³).
Torricelli: speed from a hole a depth h below the surface v = √(2gh).
Venturi meter (level pipe): P₁ − P₂ = ½ρ(v₂² − v₁²).

blocks.text: Faster flow → lower pressure: aeroplane lift, swing of a spinning ball, carburettor, spray gun.
Pipe diameter halved → area ¼ → speed × 4 (not × 2).
Laminar: smooth layers at low speed. Turbulent: eddies at high speed.

items: Condition: a = −ω²x (towards the mean position, ∝ displacement).
x = x₀ sin ωt; phase θ = ωt.
v = ω√(x₀² − x²): v_max = ωx₀ at the mean position, 0 at the ends.
a_max = ω²x₀ at the ends, 0 at the mean position.

blocks.text: Velocity is ¼ cycle (π/2) ahead of displacement; acceleration is half a cycle (π) out of phase with it.
A ball bouncing on the floor repeats its motion but is not SHM: its acceleration is not ∝ −x.
Seconds pendulum: T = 2 s, l ≈ 1 m (0.99 m). Springs: series 1/k = 1/k₁ + 1/k₂; parallel k = k₁ + k₂.
T ∝ √l: length × 4 doubles T. A spring cut in half has double k.

title: Energy in SHM, damping and resonance

items: P.E. = ½kx², K.E. = ½k(x₀² − x²), total E = ½kx₀² (constant).
E ∝ amplitude²: amplitude doubled → energy × 4.
K.E. = P.E. at x = x₀/√2.
Free oscillation: at the natural frequency, no outside force.
Damped: amplitude dies away as energy is lost to friction or drag.
Forced: driven by a periodic force at its frequency.
Resonance: driving frequency = natural frequency → maximum amplitude. Less damping → sharper, taller peak.

blocks.text: Resonance examples: tuning a radio, microwave oven heating water; soldiers break step on a bridge to avoid resonance.

title: Wave speed and the speed of sound

items: v = fλ. Transverse: string, light. Longitudinal: sound.
Wave on a string: v = √(F/μ), μ = mass per unit length.
Newton (isothermal): v = √(P/ρ) ≈ 280 m s⁻¹ in air, too low.
Laplace (adiabatic): v = √(γP/ρ) ≈ 332 m s⁻¹ at 0 °C (γ = 1.4).
v ∝ √T (kelvin); near room temperature v_t ≈ v₀ + 0.61t m s⁻¹ (t in °C).
Intensity ∝ amplitude².

blocks.text: Changing pressure at constant temperature does not change v (ρ changes with P).
Same T: v ∝ 1/√M, so sound is faster in hydrogen than in oxygen (4 times), and faster in damp air.

items: Superposition: resultant displacement = sum of the separate displacements.
Constructive: path difference = nλ. Destructive: (n + ½)λ.
Beat frequency = |f₁ − f₂|.

blocks.text: Finding an unknown fork (f = f_s ± beats)

items: Loading (wax) lowers a fork's frequency; filing raises it.
Load the unknown fork: beats decrease → it was higher; beats increase → it was lower.

blocks.text: Standard 256 Hz, 4 beats: unknown is 260 or 252 Hz. Wax on it gives 2 beats → 260 Hz.
Beats need two slightly different frequencies; equal frequencies give none.

title: Stationary waves in strings and pipes

items: Node to node = λ/2; node to next antinode = λ/4.
Fixed string end and closed pipe end: node. Open pipe end: antinode.
String: fₙ = (n/2L)√(F/μ).

blocks.text: First overtone: open pipe 2f₁, closed pipe 3f₁. A closed pipe's f₁ is half that of an open pipe of the same length.
Both moving: f′ = f(v ± u₀)/(v ∓ u_s), upper signs for approach. v = speed of sound.

items: Uses: radar speed guns, sonar, blood-flow scans, satellite tracking.
Light from a receding galaxy is red-shifted (longer λ).

blocks.text: Equal speeds of source and observer do not give the same shift: check whose formula you need.

items: Huygens: every point on a wavefront is a source of secondary wavelets; the new wavefront is their tangent (envelope).
Interference needs coherent sources (constant phase difference).
Young's double slit: fringe spacing Δy = λL/d; bright at y = nλL/d.
Reflection from an optically denser medium adds a phase change of π (path λ/2).
Thin film in air, reflected light, normal incidence: bright when 2nt = (m + ½)λ, dark when 2nt = mλ (n = film's refractive index, t = thickness).
Michelson interferometer: mirror moved L → m fringes pass, L = mλ/2.

blocks.text: Newton's rings in reflected light have a dark centre because of that π phase change.
Δy ∝ λ: red fringes are wider than blue; slits closer (smaller d) → wider fringes.

title: Diffraction: slit, grating and Bragg's law

items: Single slit of width a: first minimum at a sin θ = λ. Central maximum is the widest and brightest; narrower slit → wider pattern.
Grating: d sin θ = nλ, with d = 1/N (N = lines per metre).
Highest order: n_max = whole-number part of d/λ.
Bragg (X-rays on crystals): 2d sin θ = nλ, d = spacing of atomic planes.

blocks.text: Bragg's θ is the glancing angle (with the plane), not with the normal. Convert lines per cm to per metre: 5000 per cm → d = 2 × 10⁻⁶ m.
X-rays are used because their λ is close to atomic spacings (about 10⁻¹⁰ m).

items: Only transverse waves can be polarised, so sound cannot.
Unpolarised light through one polaroid: I = I₀/2.
Malus's law: I = I₀ cos² θ (θ between polariser and analyser axes); crossed (90°) → 0.
Light is polarised by polaroids, by reflection and by scattering.
Uses: sunglasses cutting glare, stress analysis, LCD screens, sky photography.

blocks.text: Gravitational waves: ripples in space-time from accelerating massive bodies (merging black holes or neutron stars), moving at the speed of light. Laser interferometers (LIGO) detect the tiny change in arm length; first detected in 2015.
Malus uses cos² θ, not cos θ.

items: d = least distance of distinct vision ≈ 25 cm.
M = angle subtended by the image ÷ angle by the object at the naked eye; no unit.
Lens power P = 1/f (f in metres), unit dioptre.

blocks.text: Image at infinity: simple magnifier M = d/f, not 1 + d/f. Objective image in a compound microscope: real, inverted, magnified.

title: Resolving power, speed of light and optical fibres

items: Rayleigh: smallest resolvable angle α = 1.22λ/D (radians). Larger aperture D or shorter λ → better resolution.
Spectrometer: collimator (slit at its focus gives a parallel beam), turntable, telescope.
Michelson's rotating eight-sided mirror: c = 16fd (f = revolutions per second, d = distance to the far mirror).
Optical fibre: total internal reflection; core has a higher refractive index than the cladding; at the core–cladding boundary sin C = n(cladding)/n(core) (sin C = 1/n only against air).
Fibre types: multimode step-index, multimode graded-index, single-mode.

blocks.text: A stronger eyepiece raises magnification, not resolving power: that depends only on D and λ.

items: P = ⅓ρ⟨v²⟩ = ⅓(N/V)m⟨v²⟩
PV = nRT = NkT; R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, k = R/N_A = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹
Average translational K.E. per molecule = (3/2)kT

blocks.text: Always use kelvin: 27 °C → 927 °C is 300 K → 1200 K, so v_rms doubles.
Old book Q = ΔU + W, new book ΔU = Q − W: the same law, with W = work done BY the gas.
Work = area under the P–V curve; for a cycle, the enclosed area.
An adiabatic curve is steeper than an isothermal one through the same point.

items: Constant volume: Q = nC_vΔT. Constant pressure: Q = nC_pΔT.
C_p − C_v = R; γ = C_p/C_v.
For an ideal gas ΔU = nC_vΔT in any process.

blocks.text: C_p > C_v because at constant pressure part of the heat does work PΔV as the gas expands.
These are per mole (J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹), not per kg; don't forget n.

title: Carnot engine, second law and entropy

items: Carnot cycle: two isothermals + two adiabatics.
η = 1 − T₂/T₁ = 1 − Q₂/Q₁ (kelvin); work W = Q₁ − Q₂.
Refrigerator: COP = Q₂/W = T₂/(T₁ − T₂).
Second law: no engine turns all its heat into work; heat does not flow cold → hot by itself.
Entropy ΔS = ΔQ/T (J K⁻¹). Reversible: total ΔS = 0. Irreversible (all real processes): total ΔS increases.

blocks.text: Celsius in η is the classic trap: 327 °C and 27 °C → 600 K and 300 K → η = 50%.
η depends only on T₁ and T₂, not on the working substance. Lowering T₂ helps more than raising T₁ by the same amount.

items: F = kq₁q₂/r², k = 1/4πε₀ ≈ 9 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻²
ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² C² N⁻¹ m⁻²
In a medium: F′ = F/ε_r
E = F/q₀ (N C⁻¹ = V m⁻¹); point charge E = kq/r²
Field lines leave + and end on −, never cross; closer lines = stronger field.

blocks.text: Neutral point between two like charges lies nearer the smaller charge; for unequal unlike charges it lies outside them, beyond the smaller one.
r doubled → F ÷ 4. Force on an electron is opposite to E.

items: Flux Φ = E·A = EA cos θ (N m² C⁻¹); θ between E and the area's normal.
Gauss: flux through any closed surface = q_enclosed/ε₀, whatever its shape.
Charge q at the centre of a cube: q/6ε₀ through each face.
Charged sphere: E = kq/r² outside; 0 inside a conductor or hollow shell.
Infinite sheet: E = σ/2ε₀. Between two oppositely charged plates: E = σ/ε₀.

blocks.text: No charge inside → total flux 0, even if charges sit outside. Charge on a conductor lives on its outer surface (Faraday cage).

items: V = W/q (J C⁻¹ = volt); work to move q: W = qΔV.
Point charge: V = kq/r (scalar: add with signs).
Potential gradient: E = −ΔV/Δr; parallel plates E = V/d.
Potential energy of two charges: U = kq₁q₂/r.
Millikan: oil drop held still when qV/d = mg, so q = mgd/V; every q is a whole multiple of e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.

blocks.text: V ∝ 1/r but E ∝ 1/r². Midway between equal and opposite charges V = 0 while E ≠ 0.
Equipotential surfaces are ⟂ to field lines: no work moving along them.

items: C = Q/V (farad); parallel plates C = ε_rε₀A/d.
Energy U = ½CV² = ½QV = Q²/2C.
RC circuit: time constant τ = RC (seconds).
Charging q = q₀(1 − e^(−t/RC)): 63% at t = τ.
Discharging q = q₀e^(−t/RC): 37% left at t = τ.

blocks.text: Dielectric inserted: battery connected → V fixed, Q rises; battery removed → Q fixed, V and U fall.

items: I = Q/t (A = C s⁻¹); I = nAvq (v = drift speed, very small).
Ohm's law: V = IR at constant temperature.
R = ρL/A; resistivity ρ in Ω m; conductivity σ = 1/ρ.
Series: R = R₁ + R₂ + … (same I). Parallel: 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + … (same V).

blocks.text: Wire stretched to n times its length (volume fixed): R × n². ρ depends on the material and temperature, not on the wire's shape.
Filament lamp and diode are non-ohmic: their V–I graph is not a straight line through the origin.

title: Colour code, temperature and special resistors

blocks.text: BB ROY of Great Britain has a Very Good Wife
items: Black 0, Brown 1
Red 2, Orange 3, Yellow 4
Green 5, Blue 6
Violet 7, Grey 8, White 9

blocks.text: Bands: digit, digit, multiplier (× 10ⁿ), tolerance (gold ±5%, silver ±10%, none ±20%). Brown-black-red = 10 × 10² = 1 kΩ.

items: Temperature coefficient α = (R_t − R₀)/(R₀t), unit K⁻¹; metals α > 0, carbon and semiconductors α < 0.
Thermistor (usually NTC): R falls as temperature rises.
LDR: R falls as light gets brighter.
P = VI = I²R = V²/R; 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ.
E = V + Ir; I = E/(R + r).
Terminal p.d. V = E − Ir (lost volts = Ir).
Open circuit: V = E. Short circuit: I = E/r.
Maximum power to the load when R = r: P_max = E²/4r.

blocks.text: Bulbs at the same rated V: R = V²/P, so the lower-watt bulb has more R and glows brighter in series.
A cell being charged has V = E + Ir. EMF is energy per coulomb, not a force.

items: Junction rule: ΣI = 0 (charge is conserved).
Loop rule: ΣE = ΣIR round any closed loop (energy is conserved).
Wheatstone bridge balanced (galvanometer reads 0): P/Q = R/S.
Potentiometer: comparing cells E₁/E₂ = l₁/l₂; at balance no current is drawn, so it reads the true emf.
Potential divider: V_out = V × R₂/(R₁ + R₂).

blocks.text: The bridge balance P/Q = R/S does not depend on the cell's emf or the galvanometer's resistance.
Sign slips: crossing a resistor in the direction of the current is a fall of IR; a cell crossed − to + is a rise of E. A negative answer for I just means the guessed direction was wrong.

title: Force on a current, flux density and flux

head: Quantity
Formula
SI unit
rows: T = N A⁻¹ m⁻¹ = Wb m⁻²

items: In F: θ is between wire and B. In Φ: θ is between B and the normal to the area.
1 T = 1 kg s⁻² A⁻¹ = 10⁴ gauss.
B is a vector; Φ is a scalar.
Φ = BA (greatest) when the coil's plane is ⊥ B; zero when parallel.

blocks.text: A wire lying parallel to B feels no force (sin 0° = 0). Direction: Fleming's left-hand rule.

title: Ampère's law, straight wire and solenoid

items: μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T m A⁻¹ (= Wb A⁻¹ m⁻¹); μ₀/2π = 2 × 10⁻⁷.
n = turns per metre. Inside: uniform, along the axis; outside: nearly zero.
Opposite currents inside a loop subtract: 3 A up and 5 A down enclose 2 A net.

blocks.text: Solenoid B does not depend on radius or area. Double N on the same length → 2B; double N and length → same B.

title: Charge moving in a magnetic field

items: Force: F = qvB sin θ (θ between v and B).
v ⊥ B: circle of radius r = mv/(qB) = p/(qB) = √(2mK)/(qB).
Period T = 2πm/(qB): independent of speed and radius.
e/m = v/(Br); if accelerated through V: e/m = 2V/(B²r²).
Velocity selector (E ⊥ B): undeflected when qE = qvB, so v = E/B.

blocks.text: v ∥ B: no force, straight line. The force is ⊥ v, so it does no work: speed stays constant.
Ratio questions: same v → r ∝ m/q; same KE → r ∝ √m/q; same p → r ∝ 1/q. Proton vs α at same KE: equal radii.
Electron and proton with the same velocity curve in opposite senses.

title: Torque on a coil, galvanometer, ammeter, voltmeter

items: Torque τ = BINA cos α, α = angle between the plane of the coil and B (= BINA sin θ with θ between the normal and B).
Maximum τ = BINA when the plane is parallel to B; zero when ⊥.
Galvanometer (radial field): BINA = cθ, so I ∝ θ. More sensitive with larger B, N, A or smaller c.

blocks.text: Ammeter: very low resistance. Voltmeter: very high resistance, so it draws little current.

title: Faraday's law, Lenz's law and motional EMF

items: Faraday: ε = −N ΔΦ/Δt (1 Wb s⁻¹ = 1 V).
Motional EMF of a rod: ε = vBL (v, B, L all ⊥); ε = vBL sin θ otherwise.
Induced current I = ε/R; charge that flows Q = NΔΦ/R (does not depend on time taken).
Force to pull the rod at steady speed: F = BIL = B²L²v/R.

blocks.text: Lenz: the induced current opposes the change causing it (the minus sign); this is energy conservation. Push an N pole in → that face becomes N and repels.
No flux change, no EMF: a magnet at rest in a coil, or a coil slid within a uniform field. Faster change → bigger EMF.

title: Self and mutual inductance, stored energy

blocks.text: Unit: henry, 1 H = 1 V s A⁻¹ = 1 Wb A⁻¹. Energy is stored in the magnetic field. M depends on turns, shape, separation, orientation and core.
L ∝ N²: twice the turns on the same length → 4L. Energy change from I₁ to I₂ is ½L(I₂² − I₁²), not ½L(I₂ − I₁)².

items: AC generator: ε = NωBA sin ωt, peak ε₀ = NωBA, ω = 2πf.
DC generator: same coil, split-ring commutator gives one-way output.
DC motor back EMF: V = ε_b + IR. At start ε_b = 0, so I = V/R (large).
Ideal transformer: V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p = I_p/I_s.
Efficiency = V_sI_s/(V_pI_p) × 100%.

blocks.text: Step-up for transmission: high V, low I, small I²R loss. Laminated soft-iron core: laminations cut eddy currents; soft iron cuts hysteresis loss. Thick wire on the high-current side cuts I²R heating.
A transformer never changes frequency and does not work on steady DC (no changing flux).

items: V = V₀ sin ωt, ω = 2πf; V_rms = V₀/√2 ≈ 0.707 V₀; peak-to-peak = 2V₀.
